subject: Subprocessor flow-down / proposed sideletter for Order Form 8741
messages:
From: AeroLogix <j.simmons@aerologix.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureTrust Contracts <contracts@procuretrust.com>
Date: 2026-12-13T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Subprocessor addition for Order Form 8741

Hi Marissa,

Quick heads up — AeroLogix is onboarding a new logging provider, CloudStream Inc., which will process telemetry for the integration covered under Order Form 8741. Procurement is asking us to confirm flow-down of key DPA/MSA obligations to CloudStream. Can you confirm Redwood's acceptance path and what evidence we need (SOC 2/attestation, subprocessor agreement, encryption specs)? ProcureTrust is copied for contract routing.

Thanks,
Josh Simmons
Sr. Vendor Ops | AeroLogix
Attachment: CloudStream-capabilities-summary.pdf (referenced)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: AeroLogix <j.simmons@aerologix.io>
Cc: ProcureTrust Contracts <contracts@procuretrust.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-13T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor addition for Order Form 8741

Hi Josh —

Thanks for the note. Short answer: we can accept a downstream subprocessor so long as AeroLogix ensures the flow-down of the following items in writing and provides evidence before CloudStream goes live:

- Signed subprocessor agreement or clause in CloudStream's T&Cs that mirror the data handling + security obligations in Redwood's DPA (data residency, access controls, deletion on termination).
- Current SOC 2 Type II report (last 12 months) or equivalent attestation and remediation plan for any findings.
- Confirmation of crypto-in-transit (TLS 1.2+) and at-rest encryption for telemetry buckets; key ownership model.
- A named list of CloudStream sub-subprocessors (if any) and a commitment to notify Redwood of changes.

Kimberly, I attached a draft sideletter (Sideletter-subproc-flowdown-draft-v1.docx) that we typically use to capture the flow-down commitments tied to an Order Form. Can you take a look at the DPA redlines (attached) and call out any must-haves that AeroLogix has to deliver?

Josh/ProcureTrust — would prefer to wrap this via a sideletter appended to the Order Form (no MSA amendment) unless legal tells us otherwise. Proposed timeline: evidence and signed sideletter within 10 business days. Any blockers from your side?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Sideletter-subproc-flowdown-draft-v1.docx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-13T14:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor addition for Order Form 8741

Thanks Marissa — read through the draft. High-level legal checklist:

1) Sideletter approach: OK so long as the sideletter: (a) references Order Form 8741 explicitly, (b) requires the vendor to procure identical data processing obligations from CloudStream, and (c) gives Redwood the right to require removal/replacement of the subprocessor for cause.

2) DPA redline highlights (see attached annotated PDF):
- Add explicit audit right (on-site or remote) for Redwood or its auditor for the subprocessor when processing Redwood data.
- Data breach timing: reduce vendor notification window to 48 hours for incidents impacting Redwood data.
- Subprocessor liability: carve-in specific indemnity for breaches caused by CloudStream.

3) Evidence: SOC 2 Type II is preferred; if AeroLogix provides an ISO27001 cert + penetration test report we may accept subject to a security review.

4) Escalation path: Procurement to validate commercial terms; Security (Karthik) to complete evidence review; Legal (me) to finalize sideletter language. If the vendor cannot produce SOC 2 within the timeline we should consider: temporary scoped exception with additional controls (IP allowlist, limited retention) and a firm remediation timeline.

Marissa — if AeroLogix is pushing back on audit rights we should consider adding a limited escrow/ransom recovery clause per the attached markup.

Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Attachment: DPA-redlines-annotated.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: AeroLogix <j.simmons@aerologix.io>, ProcureTrust Contracts <contracts@procuretrust.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T09:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor addition for Order Form 8741 — next steps and proposed sideletter

Josh / ProcureTrust —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached is a slightly edited sideletter that implements Kimberly's ask for explicit reference to the Order Form and the audit/notification windows. Key asks for AeroLogix/CloudStream to deliver before we approve production access:

• Signed sideletter (attached) executed by AeroLogix and CloudStream (if CloudStream requires signature).
• SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent evidence (we'll accept ISO27001 + pentest as fallback).
• Confirmation of encryption-in-transit and at-rest and the retention schedule for telemetry (max 90 days unless otherwise agreed).

If you cannot produce SOC 2 within 10 business days, please propose a temporary mitigation package including: per-tenant IP allowlist, reduced retention to 7 days, and a documented remediation plan with milestones. Legal will evaluate whether to accept a scoped exception.

ProcureTrust — once you have the signed sideletter and evidence, please upload to the contract workspace and route to DocuSign using the Order Form envelope. We will aim to lock this before the planned go-live.

Thanks,
Marissa
Attachment: Sideletter-subproc-flowdown-draft-v1.docx
From: AeroLogix <j.simmons@aerologix.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureTrust Contracts <contracts@procuretrust.com>, AeroLogix Legal <legal@aerologix.io>
Date: 2026-12-14T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor addition for Order Form 8741 — next steps and proposed sideletter

Thanks Marissa — couple of clarifying points from our side:

1) CloudStream is a managed logging layer (no user PII, only telemetry and event metadata). They are willing to sign the sideletter but request two clarifications:
   - Can the audit right be remote-first with escalation to on-site only on a defined materiality threshold?
   - Can the retention maximum be 180 days for legacy pipelines (we can confirm the majority will be 90 days, but need flexibility for a small legacy bucket)?

2) SOC 2 timeline: CloudStream's SOC 2 audit is in progress — report expected in ~6 weeks. They can provide ISO27001 + latest pentest report immediately.

3) Timeline: if we proceed with the temporary mitigation package you suggested, we can get signatures and restricted access within 7 business days.

Is remote-first audit + temporary mitigation acceptable to Redwood pending SOC2? Happy to hop on a 30-minute call today if that helps.

—Josh
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Escalation: approval request for temporary scoped exception (CloudStream)

Kimberly / Karthik / Laura —

Quick escalation to request sign-off for a temporary scoped exception so AeroLogix can proceed on the short timeline:

Context: CloudStream will not have SOC 2 available for ~6 weeks. They can provide ISO27001 + pentest now. AeroLogix offered a mitigation package:
- IP allowlist and per-tenant keys
- Reduce retention for new pipelines to 7 days; allow legacy buckets up to 180d with documented justification
- Remote-first audit right; on-site only if remote review shows material gaps

Recommendation: approve a 45-day temporary exception contingent on: (1) signed sideletter with the audit-trigger language, (2) upload of ISO27001 + pentest and remediation plan, and (3) a required SOC 2 Type II within 60 days of go-live. Procurement (Laura) to hold funds release until evidence is in workspace.

Please reply with APPROVE or DO NOT APPROVE and any edits to the contingency list. If we have approval I will instruct ProcureTrust to route DocuSign and confirm go-live gating.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Lead — Redwood Inference
